name: surfer
description: Track AI search visibility, write end-to-end articles, optimize existing content, and act on data-backed recommendations with one command.

interface.longDescription: Track traditional and AI search visibility, create and optimize content, and act on daily recommendations from Surfer directly in ChatGPT and Codex. Automate your content workflow: find your best opportunities to fix content gaps, get an outreach list of sources most cited by LLMs, generate content briefs and full pages in your brand voice, auto-optimize existing content, and run custom reports. All of Surfer’s live data in one conversation, just a few simple prompts away.
defaultPrompt: Create a Surfer outline for a keyword in my workspace.
Prepare a writer-ready content brief with Surfer guidance.
Help me optimize an existing article using Surfer.

review.commerce_description: Requires an existing Surfer account with MCP access. Usage counts toward the account's existing Surfer subscription and usage limits. This plugin does not offer subscription purchases, upgrades, or credit top-ups.

positive.description: P1. New article with outline review. Draft: reviewer setup and execution are not yet verified. Use the active workspace already selected in the conversation, verified against workspace__list. Otherwise list all pages of the connected account's active workspaces: use the sole active workspace, or ask the reviewer to choose if several are available. Stop if none is available. Do not guess a workspace or search other workspaces for better data. Required setup: brand knowledge off or a neutral publisher brand, and at least three Content Editor credits and three AI Article credits for reruns. The supplied keyword is a new-article example, not a pre-existing fixture. Resolve any workspace-selection clarification before the two task turns. Send the prompt first. Only after the assistant shows the outline and pauses, send: "Approved. Add an FAQ section at the end, then write the article." Allow approximately 10 to 20 minutes for the complete workflow.
positive.prompt: Create a new, separate SEO article for "best CRM for small businesses" in my Surfer workspace. Show me the outline and wait for my approval before writing.
positive.tools_triggered: workspace__list, content_editor__create, content_editor__get, seo_guidelines__get, ai_article__generate, ai_article__get, ai_article__get_outline, ai_article__submit_outline, content__get, content_score__get
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve the workspace as described in setup and create one new Content Editor for the requested keyword. Start one AI Article with manual_outline=true. In turn 1, retrieve the AI Article outline, show it as Markdown headings, and stop for approval without writing article text or submitting the outline. In turn 2, add the approved FAQ section to that outline, submit it, and wait for the same article to complete. Return the canonical finished article ending with an FAQ section, plus the SEO, AI Search, and total content scores from content_score__get. Read numeric scores only when ready; explicitly report failed or unavailable results instead of inventing them. The successful two-turn run consumes one Content Editor credit and one AI Article credit, with no duplicate creation or generation.

positive.description: P2. Audit an existing page. Draft: reviewer setup and execution are not yet verified. Use the active workspace already selected in the conversation, verified against workspace__list. Otherwise list all pages of the connected account's active workspaces: use the sole active workspace, or ask the reviewer to choose if several are available. Stop if none is available. Do not guess a workspace or search other workspaces for better data. Required data: at least one Content Editor created within the last 90 days that contains a full article, with SEO and AI Search analysis completed and scores ready. Use the most recently created eligible editor and identify it in the answer. Prefer a review workspace with meaningful content gaps so the run exercises actual findings. No fixed title, keyword, editor ID, or organization is required. If the required data is missing, explain what is missing without creating it or inventing results; record the positive case as blocked, not passed.
positive.prompt: Audit the most recently created Content Editor in my Surfer workspace that already contains a full article and has completed SEO and AI Search analysis. Look within the last 90 days. Tell me which editor you used and what its content is missing against both sets of guidelines. Do not change anything.
positive.tools_triggered: workspace__list, content_editor__list, content_editor__get, seo_guidelines__get_terms_coverage, ai_search_guidelines__list_facts, content__get, content_score__get
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve the workspace as described in setup. List completed Content Editors created in the last 90 days, ordered by inserted_at descending, and paginate as needed. Inspect candidates with content_editor__get and content__get; the list has no keyword, article-body, or analysis-readiness filter. Select the first eligible editor with a non-empty full article, completed SEO and AI Search analysis, and ready scores. Report its keyword and identifier. Read its term coverage, document, AI Search facts, and scores. Return recommended terms with used_count=0 and each available serp_usage.min/max suggested SERP usage range; mark a missing range as unavailable. Compare the document with the returned AI Search facts to identify uncovered facts; the facts response has no coverage flags. Attribute each uncovered fact to its returned source URL, or to its cited_by AI model when Surfer supplies no URL. Report no gaps if that is what the data supports, rather than inventing omissions. Return the ready SEO and AI Search scores as numbers supported by the tool response. Create nothing, change no content or configuration, start no generation or optimization, and spend no credits.

positive.description: P3. Writer's brief from an existing editor. Draft: reviewer setup and execution are not yet verified. Use the active workspace already selected in the conversation, verified against workspace__list. Otherwise list all pages of the connected account's active workspaces: use the sole active workspace, or ask the reviewer to choose if several are available. Stop if none is available. Do not guess a workspace or search other workspaces for better data. Required data: at least one Content Editor created within the last 90 days with a completed outline, SEO guidelines, and AI Search facts. Its document may be empty or populated; the case tests assembling a brief without writes. Use the most recently created eligible editor and take its keyword from the returned data. No fixed title, keyword, editor ID, or organization is required. If the required data is missing, explain what is missing without creating it or inventing results; record the positive case as blocked, not passed.
positive.prompt: Find the most recently created Content Editor in my Surfer workspace from the last 90 days with a completed outline, SEO guidelines, and AI Search analysis. Use its keyword and guidance to prepare a brief I can hand to a freelance writer. Tell me which editor you used. Do not create an editor, write an article, or change anything.
positive.tools_triggered: workspace__list, content_editor__list, content_editor__get, outline__get, seo_guidelines__get, ai_search_guidelines__list_facts
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve the workspace as described in setup. List completed Content Editors created in the last 90 days, ordered by inserted_at descending, and paginate as needed. Inspect content_editor__get to select the first editor whose outline, SEO guidelines, and AI Search analysis are complete; list results alone do not establish readiness. Read its outline, SEO guidelines, and AI Search facts. Report the selected editor's identifier and keyword. Return one writer-ready brief containing the keyword and search intent, the returned target word count and available structure ranges, marking unavailable values explicitly, the outline, competitor pages, recommended terms, questions to answer, and AI Search facts with the sources Surfer returned. Where a source URL is absent, preserve the cited_by model attribution without inventing a URL. Start no AI Article, create no editor, regenerate no outline, change nothing in the Content Editor, and spend no credits. Do not present a document score as evidence of the future article's quality.

positive.description: P4. AI search visibility against a discovered competitor. Draft: reviewer setup and execution are not yet verified. Use the active workspace already selected in the conversation, verified against workspace__list. Otherwise list all pages of the connected account's active workspaces: use the sole active workspace, or ask the reviewer to choose if several are available. Stop if none is available. Do not guess a workspace or search other workspaces for better data. Required data: an enabled AI Tracker project refreshed within the last day, usable reports for all five model families over the last 30 days, and at least one other brand with a non-null mention rate in the combined report. If several enabled projects are returned for the selected workspace and no project was selected, ask which project to use. The competitor is selected from live report data, not a fixed company name. If the required data is missing, explain what is missing without creating it or inventing results; record the positive case as blocked, not passed.
positive.prompt: How visible is our brand in AI search over the last 30 days in my Surfer workspace? Compare it on each AI platform with the most-mentioned other brand in the combined report. Tell me which competitor you selected and why.
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve the workspace as described in setup and identify its enabled AI Tracker project and tracked brand. Read ai_tracker__get_summary with range=30d. Read every page of ai_tracker__list_brands with range=30d and model=all until meta.total is exhausted before choosing a competitor; the API orders by presence_score, not mention_rate. Exclude the tracked brand and rows with null mention_rate. Select the other brand with the highest returned mention_rate, breaking ties alphabetically by brand_name, and explain the selection. Query ai_tracker__list_brands with range=30d for each model value ai_mode, ai_overviews, openai, perplexity, and gemini, paginating as needed to locate that same competitor; do not choose a different competitor per platform. State the actual start and end dates returned for the report window. Return one comparison table with rows for Google AI Mode, Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and all models combined. Each row shows mention rate, average position, and presence score for the tracked brand and selected competitor, using values returned for the same model and window. Label absent or null platform-specific competitor metrics as unavailable, not zero. If the project lacks the required reports or no competitor can be selected, explain the missing data and leave the case blocked. Perform reads only and spend no credits.

positive.description: P5. Plan next month's work. Draft: reviewer setup and execution are not yet verified. Use the active workspace already selected in the conversation, verified against workspace__list. Otherwise list all pages of the connected account's active workspaces: use the sole active workspace, or ask the reviewer to choose if several are available. Stop if none is available. Do not guess a workspace or search other workspaces for better data. Required data: Content Audit and a topical map refreshed within the last week, with at least three optimize recommendations and three write recommendations. No fixed domain, keyword, page URL, or organization is required. If the required data is missing, explain what is missing without creating it or inventing results; record the positive case as blocked, not passed.
positive.prompt: What should we work on next month in my Surfer workspace? Which pages should I optimize first and what should we write? Base the plan on our existing recommendations; do not start any work.
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve the workspace as described in setup. Read recommendations for that workspace with type=optimize and type=write, sort=score, and order=desc, or preserve the separately ranked type groups returned by the default mixed list. Return pages to optimize ranked by Surfer's score within the optimize type, including each returned URL, keyword, current position, and previous position. Separately rank write recommendations within the write type, including main keyword, search volume, and difficulty. To match the product display, convert raw avg_difficulty by dividing it by 100 and label the displayed scale. Do not compare scores across the two types. Every URL, keyword, and number must come from returned data; identify unavailable fields without fabricating them. Create or open no Content Editors, start no recommendation workflow or generation, change nothing, and spend no credits.

negative.description: N1. Missing keyword. Draft: execution is not yet verified. Start a fresh conversation without a keyword or prior article context. Expected behavior: ask for the keyword and, only if several workspaces are active, the workspace. Read-only workspace or recommendation discovery is allowed, including suggested keywords grounded in the account's recommendations. Do not guess and act on a keyword, create a Content Editor, start article generation or optimization, or spend credits. The request lacks the topic needed to authorize credit-consuming article creation.

N2. Unsupported deletion. Draft: execution is not yet verified. No organization name, workspace name, editor keyword, or seeded editor count is required. Expected behavior: explain that the plugin cannot delete Content Editors and deletion must be performed in the Surfer app. It may refuse without any tool call. If it chooses to inspect scope, resolve the workspace as follows: Use the active workspace already selected in the conversation, verified against workspace__list. Otherwise list all pages of the connected account's active workspaces: use the sole active workspace, or ask the reviewer to choose if several are available. Stop if none is available. Do not guess a workspace or search other workspaces for better data. Read-only discovery, counting, or an offer to list editors created in the previous calendar month is allowed, using inserted_after and inserted_before timestamps within the supported window. An empty result does not change the capability limit. Do not empty, rename, or overwrite documents as a substitute, delete templates or voices, or invoke any other write tool. No MCP tool deletes a Content Editor.
negative.prompt: Delete the Content Editors in my Surfer workspace that we created last month. We don't need them anymore.

negative.description: N3. Unsupported publishing and email. Draft: execution is not yet verified. Run with Surfer as the only enabled external integration. No fixed article title, keyword, organization, or workspace is required. A recent Content Editor with a completed AI Article is optional for exercising allowed content retrieval; the refusal must not depend on finding one. Expected behavior: explain that the Surfer plugin cannot publish to WordPress or send email, and offer or return the existing article content for the user to publish. If it retrieves content, resolve the workspace as follows: Use the active workspace already selected in the conversation, verified against workspace__list. Otherwise list all pages of the connected account's active workspaces: use the sole active workspace, or ask the reviewer to choose if several are available. Stop if none is available. Do not guess a workspace or search other workspaces for better data. List completed editors from the last 90 days in inserted_at descending order, paginate as needed, and inspect content_editor__get to find the first with ai_article.status=completed; then retrieve its content. Select by editor creation date, not an unavailable article-completion timestamp. If none exists, report that without generating one. Change nothing in Surfer, invoke no write tool or external publishing/email action, and do not claim that anything was published or sent.
negative.prompt: Find the most recently created Content Editor in my Surfer workspace from the last 90 days that contains a completed AI Article. Publish that article to our WordPress blog and email it to the team.

publication.release_notes: Initial Surfer plugin release for ChatGPT and Codex, combining the hosted Surfer MCP connection with seven skills for connection setup, article writing, content optimization, outlines, content briefs, reusable templates, and content recommendations.
